subtitle: Coins in the Dust: The Quiet Fading of the Indo-Greek Kings

panels.shot: low-angle close-up on a silver coin half-buried in dusty earth, looming mountain silhouettes and faint city walls beyond
panels.action: Hermaeus of the High Valleys stands in the far background as a distant, ghostlike figure, while in the foreground a worn Indo-Greek coin lies in the dust of a caravan road near the Hindu Kush.

dialogue.text: In the late first century before our era, Hermaeus, Hippostratos and Strato II ruled a frontier world that left no chronicles, only fading coins and the quiet memory of a vanished line of kings.

i18n.hi: पहली सदी ईसा से पहले के आख़िरी दौर में हर्मेओस, हिप्पोस्त्रातोस और स्त्रातो द्वितीय एक सरहद पर राज कर रहे थे, जहाँ से बस मिटते सिक्के बचे, न कोई इतिहास, न कोई वंशावली।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a table piled with different Indo-Greek coins under lamplight
panels.action: Hermaeus of the High Valleys, older and thoughtful, sits by a low wooden table in a dim room, his hand hovering above neat piles of silver and copper coins bearing the portraits and Greek legends of Menander, Apollodotus, Hermaeus, Hippostratos and Strato.

dialogue.text: After Menander’s time, Indo-Greek power did not fall in a single night. It splintered into small courts across Kabul, Gandhara and Punjab, their kings now known mostly from the faces and names on their coins.

i18n.hi: मेनेन्द्र के बाद इंडो-ग्रीक सत्ता एक ही रात में नहीं गिरी, वो टूटकर काबुल, गंधार और पंजाब की छोटी दरबारियों में बँट गई, जहाँ राजाओं को आज उनके सिक्कों पर बने चेहरों और नामों से पहचाना जाता है।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye wide of mountain passes with tiny caravans moving through
panels.action: Hermaeus stands on a rocky outcrop above a narrow pass in the Paropamisadae, snow-tipped peaks around him and a thin line of pack animals winding below, hinting at the Kabul valley routes between Central Asia and the Indian plains.

dialogue.text: Hermaeus held the high valleys of Paropamisadae and the Kabul region, where the winds of Central Asia met the roads to India. To the east in Gandhara and Punjab, Hippostratos and the Strato line ruled their own contested frontiers.

i18n.hi: हर्मेओस ने पारोपामिसादे और काबुल की ऊँची घाटियाँ थाम रखी थीं, जहाँ मध्य एशिया की हवा भारत की सड़कों से मिलती थी; उधर गंधार और पंजाब में हिप्पोस्त्रातोस और स्त्रातो वंश अपनी-अपनी टकराती सरहदें संभाल रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Hermaeus examining a newly struck coin by a mint furnace
panels.action: In a simple mint courtyard, Hermaeus watches a die-engraver and a hammerman at work; a glowing metal blank is struck and a new coin flies into a tray showing his diademed head and a standing Athena, the Greek and Kharoshthi legends tiny but clear.

dialogue.text: No Greek historian wrote his story. Yet Hermaeus’ reign is traced in silver: coins with his name in Greek and Kharoshthi, his portrait facing deities and symbols that still carried the memory of Alexander’s successors.

i18n.hi: उसकी कहानी कोई यूनानी इतिहासकार नहीं लिख गया, पर हर्मेओस की हुकूमत चाँदी में दिखती है — सिक्कों पर उसका नाम यूनानी और खरोष्ठी में, उसका चेहरा देवताओं और उन निशानों के सामने जो अब भी सिकंदर के उत्तराधिकारियों की याद लिए हुए हैं।

panels.shot: split composition: one side a Punjab plain city, the other a frontier outpost, both linked by a faint map overlay
panels.action: Hermaeus stands on one side against a rugged hill fortress backdrop, while on the other he appears again symbolically as Hippostratos and Strato II, presiding over walled towns on the Punjab plain; faint river lines and dotted borders hint at overlapping little kingdoms.

dialogue.text: Numismatists like Bopearachchi and R. C. Senior piece together this late Indo-Greek mosaic. Hermaeus in the west, Hippostratos and Apollodotus II in central Punjab, Strato II and III further east, their realms overlapping like the circles of their scattered coin finds.

i18n.hi: बोपेराची और आर. सी. सीनियर जैसे मुद्राशास्त्री इस आख़िरी इंडो-ग्रीक तस्वीर को जोड़ते हैं — पश्चिम में हर्मेओस, मध्य पंजाब में हिप्पोस्त्रातोस और अपोल्लोदोतुस द्वितीय, और आगे पूरब में स्त्रातो द्वितीय व तृतीय, जिनकी रियासतें बिखरे सिक्कों के घेरे की तरह एक-दूसरे पर चढ़ती दिखती हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a dusty frontier market with mixed peoples, low camera among traders’ legs
panels.action: Hermaeus moves anonymously through a bustling border market filled with Greek-looking soldiers, Indian farmers, Saka horsemen and Parthian-style merchants, as coins pass from palm to palm over scales and bales of goods.

dialogue.text: Their courts were not towers of pure Hellenism. Markets in Kabul and Gandhara rang with Greek, Prakrit and Iranian tongues; their coins bore Greek gods and Indian symbols, serving caravan trade that linked Bactria, the Indus and beyond.

i18n.hi: उनके दरबार शुद्ध हेल्लेनिक मीनारें नहीं थे; काबुल और गंधार की मंडियों में यूनानी, प्राकृत और ईरानी ज़ुबानें गूँजती थीं, सिक्कों पर यूनानी देवता और भारतीय चिह्न, जो कारवाँ के उस व्यापार की सेवा करते थे जो बाक्ट्रिया से सिन्धु और आगे तक जाता था।

panels.shot: medium wide of a council hall where Hermaeus listens to a Saka envoy
panels.action: In a modest wooden hall, Hermaeus sits on a low throne while a tall, fur-capped Saka chieftain with a bow across his back gestures calmly, flanked by horsemen; Indo-Greek officers in mixed gear watch tensely.

dialogue.text: From the north and west came new powers. Saka groups moved down from the steppes, and Indo-Parthian leaders pressed in. The coins show their influence too, as later issues blend Indo-Greek legends with the names and symbols of incoming rulers.

i18n.hi: उत्तर और पश्चिम से नई ताक़तें उतरीं; साका झुंड घास के मैदानों से नीचे आए और इंडो-पार्थियन सरदार दबाव बनाने लगे; उनके असर भी सिक्कों पर दिखते हैं, जहाँ बाद के टकसालों में इंडो-ग्रीक लेखों के साथ नए शासकों के नाम और निशान घुलमिल जाते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of a Hermaeus coin overstruck with a different king’s name
panels.action: A gloved hand holds a struck coin close; the faint original portrait and name of Hermaeus can still be seen beneath a newer design and legend bearing a different ruler, symbolising overstriking and succession.

dialogue.text: In some cases, later Saka and Indo-Parthian kings struck their designs over Hermaeus’ types. The older Greek name still whispers beneath, showing not a sudden conquest we can date, but a gradual folding of his realm into theirs.

i18n.hi: कई जगह बाद के साका और इंडो-पार्थियन राजाओं ने अपने डिज़ाइन हर्मेओस के सिक्कों पर चढ़ाकर मारे, पुराने यूनानी नाम नीचे हल्का-सा फुसफुसाता रह गया, जो किसी साफ़ तारीख़ वाली जंग नहीं, बल्कि उसके राज्य के धीरे-धीरे उनके में घुल जाने की तरफ़ इशारा करता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Punjab city gate where Greek soldiers share watch with Saka and Parthian-style warriors
panels.action: On a warm Punjab morning, Hermaeus as Hippostratos-like figure walks along a city wall as mixed guards—some in Hellenistic helmets, others in steppe caps and Parthian coats—stand together looking out over the fields.

dialogue.text: Hippostratos in the Punjab also faced Saka advance. His coins show Greek legends paired with Indian scripts and a variety of symbols. They taper off as Saka rulers with names like Azes come to dominate the same regions in the numismatic record.

i18n.hi: पंजाब का हिप्पोस्त्रातोस भी साका बढ़त से जूझ रहा था; उसके सिक्कों पर यूनानी लिखावट भारतीय लिपियों और तरह-तरह के चिह्नों के साथ जुड़ी दिखती है, मगर जैसे-जैसे आज़ेस जैसे नामों वाले साका शासक वही इलाक़े सिक्कों से भरने लगे, उसकी टकसालें पतली पड़ती गईं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Strato II in a small court, studying an older coin of Menander
panels.action: In an eastern Punjab palace courtyard, Strato II, wearier and more modestly dressed than earlier Indo-Greek kings, holds up an old, slightly worn coin of Menander, its legend still visible, while attendants and scribes stand by with account tablets.

dialogue.speaker: hermaeus_hippostratos_and_strato_ii
dialogue.text: Menander’s silver still pays our soldiers. But their loyalty follows the strongest rider.

i18n.hi: मेनेन्द्र की चाँदी से अभी हमारे सिपाहियों की तनख़्वाह चलती है, पर उनकी वफ़ादारी सबसे मज़बूत घुड़सवार के पीछे जाती है।

panels.shot: close-up on a ledger tablet and bowls where different kings’ coins are sorted
panels.action: Hands sort coins into small bowls marked only by their arrangements, while a scribe etches notes on a palm-leaf; coins of Apollodotus II, Strato II and Saka kings lie mixed, some fresh, some worn smooth.

dialogue.text: Strato II’s issues often show reduced silver content and crude engraving beside earlier pieces. The shrinking weight and artistry hint at strain, as eastern fragments of the Indo-Greek realm endured under pressure and perhaps shrinking revenues.

i18n.hi: स्त्रातो द्वितीय के सिक्कों में अक्सर कम चाँदी और पहले की तुलना में कच्ची नक़्क़ाशी दिखती है; घटता वज़न और बिगड़ती कला बताती है कि पूर्वी इंडो-ग्रीक टुकड़े दबाव और शायद घटती आमदनी के बीच किसी तरह टिके हुए थे।

panels.shot: soft-focus interior of a Gandharan workshop where an artisan carves a Buddha in Hellenistic-influenced style
panels.action: Hermaeus watches quietly from the doorway of a Gandharan atelier where an Indian sculptor, guided by a half-Greek, half-Indian master, chisels a serene Buddha figure with flowing drapery reminiscent of Greek robes and realistic folds.

dialogue.text: While their power waned, artistic currents in Gandhara drew on their heritage. In later centuries, Buddhas in Gandharan stone would wear draperies and poses shaped in part by Hellenistic forms, though the later sculptors no longer named the kings who had once ruled there.

i18n.hi: शक्ति घटती गई, पर गंधार की कला धाराएँ उनकी विरासत से रस खींचती रहीं; सदियों बाद गंधार की पत्थर की बुद्ध प्रतिमाएँ ऐसे वस्त्र और मुद्राएँ अपनाएँगी जिनमें कहीं न कहीं हेल्लेनिस्टिक रूपों की झलक होगी, भले ही उन कलाकारों को अब उन पुराने राजाओं के नाम तक याद न हों।

panels.shot: wide shot of a caravan at an Indian Ocean port, with merchants examining old coins
panels.action: On a sunlit western Indian harbour, perhaps on the Gujarat coast, foreign and Indian traders cluster around a small table where an older merchant displays worn coins of Menander and Apollodotus alongside newer Saka types, ships’ masts rising behind them.

dialogue.text: Far to the south and west, the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, written in the first century CE, still remembered the fine coins of Menander and Apollodotus in coastal trade. Long after their dynasties vanished, their names survived as trusted money.

i18n.hi: बहुत दक्षिण और पश्चिम में, पहली सदी ईस्वी का ‘एरिथ्रैयन सागर का पेरिप्लस’ अब भी समुद्री व्यापार में मेनेन्द्र और अपोल्लोदोतुस के बढ़िया सिक्कों को याद करता है, यानी राजवंश मिट गए, पर उनके नाम भरोसेमंद मुद्रा की तरह जीवित रहे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Hermaeus alone in a dim hall, with maps and spears in shadow
panels.action: Hermaeus stands in a nearly empty audience hall, maps rolled on the floor and spears stacked unused in the corners, light from a high slit window striping his face as he contemplates the quiet.

dialogue.text: For Hermaeus, Hippostratos and Strato II, there is no recorded last stand, no chronicler’s date where the curtain falls. Their coins simply cease, replaced by Saka and Indo-Parthian issues, as if the Greek names slipped out of common speech.

i18n.hi: हर्मेओस, हिप्पोस्त्रातोस और स्त्रातो द्वितीय के लिए कोई लिखी आख़िरी लड़ाई नहीं, न कोई तारीख़ जहाँ परदा गिरा हो; बस उनके सिक्के रुक जाते हैं, जगह ले लेते हैं साका और इंडो-पार्थियन टकसालें, जैसे यूनानी नाम धीरे-धीरे आम ज़ुबान से फिसल गए हों।

panels.shot: close-up on Hermaeus’ hand placing his coin beside a Saka king’s coin on a stone
panels.action: In an intimate moment, Hermaeus’ hand lays one of his own bright silver pieces on a stone ledge, next to a heavier coin bearing a Saka ruler’s name and a mounted horseman, the two disks touching edge to edge.

i18n.hi: नाम बदलते हैं, राहें रहती हैं।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot of the same frontier landscape across decades, people and banners changing
panels.action: The same river valley and hill fortress are shown as seasons seem to wheel past: first Indo-Greek standards fly, then Saka banners, then later forms, while Hermaeus’ figure grows fainter in successive ghostly overlays.

dialogue.text: Over a few generations the Indo-Greek courts were absorbed, their soldiers perhaps hired under new chiefs, their mints turned to fresh names. The frontier landscape stayed busy, but the line of Hermaeus and Strato dissolved into larger powers.

i18n.hi: कुल दो–तीन पीढ़ियों में इंडो-ग्रीक दरबार समा गए; उनके सिपाही शायद नए सरदारों की नौकरी में, उनकी टकसालें नए नामों के लिए; सरहद का मंजर उतना ही रौनक भरा रहा, पर हर्मेओस और स्त्रातो की लाइन बड़ी ताक़तों में घुलकर मिट गई।

panels.shot: modern-leaning shot of an archaeologist’s hand brushing soil from an Indo-Greek coin in a dig trench
panels.action: Centuries later, a modern excavator’s hand gently reveals an Indo-Greek coin—its king’s head and Greek letters emerging from packed earth in a trench, while Hermaeus appears faintly in the background as a translucent figure watching.

dialogue.text: Today, it is archaeologists and numismatists who give them back a voice. Hermaeus, Hippostratos and Strato II emerge not from epic poems, but from excavation pits, museum trays and careful reconstructions of scattered hoards.

i18n.hi: आज पुरातत्वविद और मुद्राशास्त्री ही उन्हें फिर आवाज़ देते हैं; हर्मेओस, हिप्पोस्त्रातोस और स्त्रातो द्वितीय महाकाव्यों से नहीं, खुदाई के गड्ढों, संग्रहालय की तश्तरियों और बिखरी थैलियों की सूझ-बूझ भरी जोड़तोड़ से उभरते हैं।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of Hermaeus’ weathered face dissolving into the worn profile on a coin
panels.action: Hermaeus’ lined, thoughtful face fills the frame, then subtly merges into the profile on a heavily worn coin, the features nearly smoothed away yet still just recognisable under the play of light.

dialogue.text: Their story reminds us that some kingdoms end not with a single battle, but with quiet absorption—names fading from use while coins, roads and art carry small traces of them far beyond their own age.

i18n.hi: उनकी कहानी याद दिलाती है कि कुछ राज्य किसी एक बड़ी जंग से नहीं, बल्कि चुपचाप समा जाने से खत्म होते हैं — जब नाम ज़ुबान से मिटते जाते हैं, पर सिक्कों, सड़कों और कला में उनके हल्के निशान अपनी उम्र से बहुत आगे तक चल देते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: Coins in the Dust: The Quiet Fading of the Indo-Greek Kings
subtitle_i18n.hi: धूल में सिक्के: चुपचाप ढलते इंडो-ग्रीक राजे
